sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: regional transport engagement officer: announce a reviewable demonstration

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the route atlas and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The consultation file review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I arranged a school-route consultation once the affected stops and operator contacts were listed.
Was demand still unmeasured?
No, families had identified pickup points and the operator shared ridership counts.
Someone new shadowed me in the mobility office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the service reviews into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the consultation file records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I updated the route atlas after the operator confirmed a temporary diversion boundary.
Did that announce a permanent shuttle?
No, it recorded a short operational change.
I archived last cycle's notes on the consultation file and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The mobility fund includes money for a travel diary exercise and a one-month demonstration service.
Does that establish a permanent route?
No, it lets us gather demand and operating evidence.
A vendor call about the route atlas ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the mobility office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the service reviews.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the consultation file records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine service reviews cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the service reviews before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the route atlas updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The council transport committee meets after the demonstration period.
Why is that useful?
It provides a place to consider the evidence before any lasting commitment.
I compared two options for the consultation file tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the mobility office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Can I announce a one-month hill-district shuttle demonstration?

query: Can I announce a one-month hill-district shuttle demonstration?

ev_A.fact: When the hill-district shuttle idea arrived with resident requests and a rough corridor but no stop-level demand counts or operator view of turning constraints, I told the committee we could announce a one-month demonstration and diary review, not a permanent route pattern.

ev_B.fact: On a valley loop consultation, I pledged a permanent route before the operator shared turning assessments; mid-trial the service had to be withdrawn when a narrow corner could not be safely repeated.

E1.fact: The mobility fund includes money for a travel diary exercise and a one-month demonstration service.

E2.fact: The council transport committee meets after the demonstration period.

relational_connector.relation: The hill-district triage episode shows a defensible public commitment the current file can support, while the valley loop pledge episode shows why a permanent route cannot be promised before turning and demand evidence exists.
